prerequisites: Completion of Psychology of Education and Pedagogy I courses

learning_outcomes.text: Presents domain-specific contents and correlates main theories and methodological orientations of learning from the perspective of pedagogical design.
Argues the relationships between teaching-learning-evaluation and formulates creative solutions for optimizing educational components.
Applies specific didactic principles and methods to educational activities that ensure the progress of children/students/young people/other categories of people.
Explains the specific formative potential of didactic strategies, methods, procedures, didactic means, and digital technologies.

Presents the principles, roles, functions, and purposes of evaluation, as well as evaluation methods and instruments correlated with the type of activity and developmental stage of children/students/young people.
Describes and correlates the main methods and instruments for evaluating/self-evaluating school results.
Uses specialized, psychopedagogical knowledge within the entire pedagogical process of designing educational activities and resources.
Applies didactic principles and strategies in designing educational activities specific to the age level and group being worked with.
Identifies the level of previous individual and group acquisitions of children/students/young people, and uses the obtained data in designing the educational process.
Develops models for designing educational activities or pedagogical design, integrating innovative resources.

Develops diverse contexts in designing didactic activity, in which children/students/young people can demonstrate progress in competence development, facilitating self-evaluation, reflection, and setting new learning objectives.
Uses diverse, creative, and efficient didactic strategies (teaching, learning, evaluation) to facilitate the learning progress of each student.
Builds authentic learning contexts, in an integrated manner, in which students utilize their life experiences and knowledge interests.
Uses a wide range of evaluation methods and instruments for recording, analyzing, and communicating evaluation results, specific to the domain.
Evaluates the effectiveness of the strategies used and their impact on children/students/young people/groups by referring to standards and objectives mentioned in curricular documents.
Develops models for recording evaluation results, individually and for groups, according to the age (and individual) peculiarities of children/students/young people.
Critically approaches the responsibilities of the teaching profession, highlighting the complexity of the educational process.
Develops creative and constructive attitudes in applying the design of pedagogical principles.
Organizes educational activities in compliance with the principles and specific methodologies of didactics applied in education (for any type/category of children/students/young people/groups).
Indicates the necessity of using varied resources for efficient teaching, supporting learning, and helping students in their autonomous use.
Consistently applies didactic approaches that support the development of literacy, numeracy, digital, and civic competences.
Communicates efficiently by providing constructive feedback and supports active student involvement in their own learning process.
Uses information obtained from evaluations to optimize the educational process, critically analyze activities, and make ameliorative decisions.
Conducts evaluations and self-evaluations of educational activity in compliance with ethical and professional deontology norms.

syllabus_topics: The teaching-learning process.
Didactic principles.
Didactic strategy: didactic methods, didactic means, forms of organization. Online teaching methods.
Forms of organizing the teaching-learning process. Theory and practice of the lesson.
Didactic design.
Didactic evaluation: the concept of evaluation in education, functions and operations of evaluation.
Types of evaluation within the teaching-learning process.
Traditional evaluation methods. Complementary evaluation methods. Digital evaluation methods/applications.
Evaluation tests: test drafting; item elaboration techniques; grading rubric elaboration.
Assessment of school results. Distortions (errors) in assessing school results. Ways to prevent and reduce variability in grading.
Course presentation, topics, bibliography, explanation of how seminar didactic activities are carried out. The teaching-learning process - its formative-educational character.
Interrelations teaching-learning-evaluation, traditional and modern meanings. Forms and factors of teaching. Identifying and analyzing one's own learning styles.
The system of didactic principles. Case studies.
The system of didactic methods - exemplification in learning sequences: traditional methods; modern methods based on interactivity.

Forms of organizing the teaching-learning process. Theory and practice of the lesson - organization by classes and by lessons; methodological requirements in organization and conduct; types and variants of lessons - exemplification.
Didactic design. Exercises in designing didactic activities.
Evaluation in the teaching-learning process: functions of evaluation, structure of the act of evaluation measurement. Forms of evaluation - initial, continuous, final.
Methods and techniques of evaluation: traditional and complementary.
Evaluation tests: elaboration exercises.
Assessment of school results. Distortions (errors) in assessing school results. Case studies.
teaching_methods: Traditional didactic methods (exposure; conversation; case study; problematization; role-playing, etc.)
Interactive methods (mosaic; Frisco technique; pyramid method; reciprocal teaching-learning, etc.)
Didactic means (Power Point presentations; digital applications for knowledge systematization and recapitulation; worksheets; documentary films, etc.)

Organization of didactic activity respecting the design of adult education activities, integrating new knowledge with previously transmitted knowledge, utilizing students' learning/life experience in the analysis of proposed applications.
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result requires a minimum final grade of 5.
